title: Real-Time Policy Enforcement: Palo Alto Networks Firewalls Integrate with AWS Transit Gateway Context Sharing
summary: We are excited to announce the integration of Palo Alto Networks firewalls with AWS Transit Gateway Resource Context Sharing. This integration delivers
body_markdown:
[Announcement](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/category/announcement/)


[Partners](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/category/partners/)


[Products and Services](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/category/products-and-services/)


We are excited to announce the integration of Palo Alto Networks firewalls with AWS Transit Gateway Resource Context Sharing. This integration delivers AWS resource context directly to the firewalls, enabling you to enforce real-time, tag-based policies that secure dynamic, auto-scaling public cloud environments without friction or slowdown.


First, some background: As organizations adopt AI to accelerate innovation, threat actors[weaponize](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/autonomous-ai-cyber-attack-campaign/) the same technologies to automate reconnaissance and launch targeted campaigns at machine speed. These attacks impact organizations[in minutes rather than days](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/resources/research/unit-42-incident-response-report#inside-the-intrustion-3) . With more than half of these threats driven via the network, your organization needs real-time, network-based threat prevention.


Enforcing this real-time protection is uniquely challenging in dynamic cloud environments, making this integration critical. Modern cloud environments have ephemeral workloads, such as auto-scaling sets of instances, containers, and serverless functions, that spin up, run, and spin down in minutes or less. To secure these environments against fast-moving threats, your security teams author Palo Alto Networks firewall policies for collections of AWS workloads grouped by their assigned[cloud tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/tagging-best-practices/what-are-tags.html) . These policies secure traffic based on a workload's logical identity rather than relying on static, quickly outdated IP addresses. This workload identity-based approach ensures dynamic security enforcement as workloads are added or removed from the group.


## The Problem: The Synchronization Gap and Operational Friction


Until now, mapping a newly spawned dynamic IP address to its corresponding cloud tag required an out-of-band synchronization. Palo Alto Networks management layers (like Panorama and Strata Cloud Manager) would periodically poll the AWS APIs to harvest these IP-to-tag mappings and push them to the firewalls.


**Figure 1: The Synchronization Gap:** Out-of-band API polling incurs delay, forcing a tradeoff between deploying workloads quickly and securing them immediately.


This polling cycle can take several minutes to synchronize, forcing you into an unacceptable tradeoff between business **velocity and risk** . If your security team enforces a strict Zero Trust posture, the firewall will block the unknown IPs of newly spun-up workloads. This breaks application traffic, disrupts user experiences, and creates friction with application teams. Alternatively, if the policy allows the traffic through until the tag is identified, it creates a security blind spot that attackers can exploit to move laterally.


## AWS Transit Gateway Context Sharing Changes the Game


With the launch of *AWS Transit Gateway context sharing* , you no longer have to make the compromise. It integrates seamlessly with Palo Alto Networks firewalls' in-band tags to close the synchronization gap. AWS now embeds resource context directly into the traffic it sends to your firewall, shifting workload context from a reactive, out-of-band process to a proactive, inline capability. This means your security team no longer has to play catch-up via APIs.


**Figure 2: Security at Speed and Scale:** AWS embeds context directly into network traffic, protecting dynamic workloads without compromising on speed or scale.


## What Context is Shared?


When you use AWS Transit Gateway to centralize your security alongside Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to scale the firewall infrastructure, AWS now shares specific tags as resource context metadata seamlessly through GENEVE Type-Length-Values (TLVs). When traffic reaches the Palo Alto Networks firewall, it extracts the context inline and instantly recognizes critical metadata such as Amazon VPC, subnet, and security-group IDs. The context also includes Transit Gateway attachment IDs and Region IDs.


**Figure 3: Real-Time Policy Enforcement:** Palo Alto Networks firewalls extract the inline metadata from the very first packet to deliver instant, agentless micro-segmentation.


To utilize this capability, simply connect your Palo Alto Networks firewalls to an AWS Transit Gateway as a[network function attachment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-nf-fw.html) , and then create a context store to maintain context for your attached VPCs and on-premises resources. With the integration enabled, you can author in-band tag security policies directly in Panorama. Because the firewall instantly recognizes the AWS resource context embedded in the traffic header, it enforces the corresponding in-band tag policy from the very first packet. For step-by-step instructions, refer to the[AWS blog post](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/introducing-resource-context-for-firewall-policies-with-aws-transit-gateway/) and the[demonstration video](https://youtu.be/op5mGU0UdKY) .


## Three Ways the Integration Pays Off


Palo Alto Networks software firewall integration with AWS Resource Context Sharing offers the following strategic benefits:


- **Security at Speed and Scale** – You can now secure traffic from cloud workloads as soon as they boot up. Application teams can deploy and scale applications at the speed of the cloud, knowing the security infrastructure will protect them by enforcing security policies from the very first packet they send.
- **Scalable, Agentless Architecture** – Easily define and enforce scalable micro-segments and reduce the attack surface, without the heavy operational burden of managing host-based agents.
- **Streamlined Governance** – Gain deterministic, packet-level visibility into exactly which AWS segments or security groups triggered specific firewall rules. This eliminates guesswork, drastically reduces Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR), and simplifies compliance audits.


> Our customers demand security that moves at the speed of the cloud. By integrating Software Firewalls’ In-band tags feature with the AWS Transit Gateway context sharing, we empower enterprises to secure ephemeral workloads the moment they boot up.


***Rich Campagna***
*SVP of Product Management at Palo Alto Networks*


> AWS gives customers the flexibility to secure their environments with the firewall of your choice, and we work closely with partners like Palo Alto Networks to make those firewalls work better on AWS. Customers use VPCs, subnets, and security groups to define how workloads are grouped and secured on AWS. AWS Transit Gateway now carries that resource context to firewalls with the traffic, giving customers a simpler way to write network segmentation policies while continuing to use existing IP-based policies. This is another example of how we work with partners to make security on AWS stronger and easier to manage.


***Robert Kennedy***
*Vice President of Network Services at AWS*


The Software Firewall In-band tags feature is now available in Palo Alto Networks self-managed firewalls (VM-Series, Prisma AIRS AI Runtime Security). It will be available next year in Palo Alto Networks Managed firewalls (Cloud NGFW, Managed AI Runtime Security). This collaboration underscores both organizations' commitment to providing cloud-native, customer-centric solutions that empower businesses with best-in-class security and that are easy to deploy and manage.


In a landscape where AI-driven attacks operate at machine speed in the order of minutes, your defenses should stop compromising between cloud velocity and robust security. Activate AWS Transit Gateway context sharing today and configure in-band policies in your Palo Alto Networks firewalls to secure traffic from ephemeral workloads as soon as they boot up. You can easily procure and deploy our firewalls directly through our[AWS Marketplace Listings](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/seller-profile?id=0ed48363-5064-4d47-b41b-a53f7c937314) .
